headline: Smithsonian's Smallest Museum Keeps DC Stories Alive
meta_description: A tiny Smithsonian museum has spent nearly six decades preserving and sharing the stories of Washington, DC's diverse communities.
summary_short: For nearly 60 years, the Smithsonian's smallest museum has quietly preserved the voices and histories of Washington, DC residents.
body:
For nearly six decades, the Smithsonian's smallest museum has served as a keeper of stories—documenting and celebrating the lives of Washington, DC's residents.

This modest institution stands as proof that a museum doesn't need grand halls or sprawling galleries to make a meaningful impact. By focusing intently on the people of Washington, DC, it has carved out a vital niche within one of the world's most prestigious museum networks, ensuring that local voices and community histories aren't lost to time.

The museum's longevity speaks to the enduring hunger for spaces where ordinary people's extraordinary stories can be heard, preserved, and honored for generations to come.
